text:
sam: morning — observability flagged a steady rise in tiny-pod evictions in ap-east1 starting ~00:40 UTC, looks like pack scatter across racks. heatmap: https://redwood.internal/gpu/heatmap?region=ap-east1

lynn: yup, noticed embedder tiny pods with PodAntiAffinity are spreading and leaving 0.5-1 GPU holes on many nodes. eviction_count = +240 over last 2h.

raj: I pulled scheduler metrics, `scheduler_scheduling_attempts` spiked and `pod_evictions_total` correlates. many evictions labelled "InsufficientResources" after transient NodeReady flaps.

infra-bot: [ANOMALY] ap-east1 rack skew detected. stranded_gpus_estimate: 22. suggested_action: descheduler run targeting pods with annotation `tiny-gpu=true`.

tess: what's the root cause? NIC, kubelet, or scheduler policy?

sam: digging into node events: `NetworkUnreachable` messages across a handful of nodes in rack-7 between 00:35-00:42. Also saw kubelet restarts 00:41 on node gpu-rack7-node3.

lynn: that matches — transient node NotReady -> scheduler quickly backfills replicas onto other racks (respecting anti-affinity), which leads to fragmentation. scheduler is probably honoring `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` too strictly for tiny pods.

raj: examples from logs:
```
I0301 00:41:05.123 scheduler_pred: pod embedder-xyz failed predicate PodFitsResources: Insufficient resources
I0301 00:41:07.456 kubelet: NodeNotReady
I0301 00:41:09.789 controller: evicted pod embedder-abc due to NodeAffinity/NetworkUnreachable
```

infra-bot: runbook reminder: consider soft-pack policy + descheduler instead of mass drains during transient faults.

sam: proposal: 1) launch descheduler canary in ap-east1-rack-a targeting pods with `tiny-gpu=true` and priorityClass < standard, eviction cap per node = 2, 2) set a short autoscaler placement-suppress for new tiny pod replicas in rack-7, 3) tag flaky nodes `investigate/network` and queue firmware ticket if repeats.

lynn: +1 on canary. also recommend creating a temporary scheduler plugin tweak: relax anti-affinity scoring for pods with label `tiny-pack-eligible=true` so they prefer denser placement when network anomalies occur. low-risk toggle for 30m.

raj: canary descheduler yaml I used before:
```
apiVersion: descheduler/v1
kind: PodDeschedulerPolicy
strategies:
  EvictPods:
    enabled: true
    params:
      podSelectors:
      - labelSelector: "tiny-gpu=true"
        evictLocalStoragePods: false
      maxPodsToEvictPerNode: 2
```

tess: watch out for warmpool pressure — we already had two warmpool nodes with high CPU after previous consolidation. set `maxUnreadyPercent` so we don't over-consolidate.

sam: noted — will set `maxUnreadyPercent=25` in descheduler job. launching canary now in ap-east1-a.

ops-bot: descheduler-canary deployed in ap-east1-a at 00:53 UTC. job-id: ds-1713749999-canary

lynn: results after 12m: evicted ~18 tiny pods, consolidated into 7 nodes, freed 9 GPUs in rack-7 and rack-8. p95 latency for embedder unchanged. warmpool cpu spike +6% for 10m then back to baseline.

raj: good. next: cordon the 4 nodes with repeated NIC flaps in rack-7 and drain once descheduler finishes relocating pods. that'll allow hardware team to run NIC health checks without churn.

sam: I'm going to push a temporary placement-suppress CA policy to avoid placing new tiny pods into rack-7 for 20m. command: `kubectl annotate cluster autoscaler redwood placement-suppress=ap-east1-rack-7:20m`

infra-bot: incident placeholder created: INC-2026-0361. severity: sev3. assigned: eng-platform.

tess: cost note — short-term consolidation increases on-demand GPU burst; estimate +$25/hr during consolidation window. will log in incident. still cheaper than SLA breach.

lynn: after cordon+drain of 3/4 flapped nodes, evictions dropped back to baseline. left one node cordoned for hardware debug.

raj: postmortem notes to include: 1) transient NIC flaps caused by firmware regression on Mellanox driver, 2) scheduler reactivity amplified fragmentation for tiny pods with anti-affinity, 3) mitigations: firmware roll, scheduler scoring tweak for tiny pods, and a descheduler-based auto-defrag job when stranded_gpus > threshold.

sam: action items: raj -> open firmware ticket with infra-hardware and provide node list; lynn -> PR for scheduler config toggle (tiny-pack-eligible scoring); tess -> record cost impact in incident; ops-bot -> schedule descheduler recurring check when stranded_gpus > 10.

ops-bot: scheduled task `auto-defrag-check` to run every 15m in ap-east1. threshold: stranded_gpus >= 10.

sam: thanks everyone. closing for now, reopen if metrics regress. :thumbsup:
